4386.stem:
A table of future value interest factors for an annuity of \$1 is shown.

\extable{300_q25_t1}

parts.latex:
Micky wants to save \$450 000 over the next 10 years.

If the interest rate is $6\%$ per annum compounding annually, how much should Micky contribute each year? Give your answer to the nearest dollar.

Instead, Micky decides to contribute \$8535 every three months for 10 years to an annuity paying $6\%$ per annum, compounding quarterly.

How much will Micky have at the end of 10 years?

solutions.latex:
For 10 periods at 6%, the table factor is $13.181$. Each contribution is the target divided by the factor.
$$\begin{aligned}\text{Contribution} &= \dfrac{\$450\,000}{13.181} \\ &\approx \$34\,140\end{aligned}$$
to the nearest dollar.
criteria: Correct answer
Identifies the correct factor from the table

solutions.latex:
Quarterly compounding gives the rate per period:
$$\begin{aligned}r &= \dfrac{6}{4}\% \\ &= 1.5\%\end{aligned}$$
Number of periods:
$$\begin{aligned}n &= 10\times 4 \\ &= 40\end{aligned}$$
From the table, the factor for $1.5\%$ and 40 periods is $54.268$.
$$\begin{aligned}\text{Amount} &= \$8535\times 54.268 \\ &= \$463\,177.38\end{aligned}$$
criteria: Correct answer
Provides the correct interest rate and the correct number of periods, or equivalent merit
Multiplies a factor from the table by $\$8535$, or equivalent merit

parts.latex: How much does Zal need to deposit every year if he wishes to have enough money for the trip in 4 years time?
How much interest will Zal earn on his investment over the 4 years? Give your answer to the nearest dollar.

solutions.latex:
The table factor for $3\%$ over 4 years is $4.184$.
$$\begin{aligned} \text{Deposit} &= \$15\,000 \div 4.184 \\ &= \$3585.09 \end{aligned}$$
criteria: Correct answer
Finds the correct interest factor, or equivalent merit
Correct answer
Finds the total amount deposited, or equivalent merit

parts.latex: What is the value of Eli's investment after 10 years using Option 1?
What is the difference between the future values after 10 years using Option 1 and Option 2?

solutions.latex:
Here $P = 40\,000$, $r = 1.2\%$ per annum compounded monthly, and $N = 10 \times 12 = 120$.
$$\begin{aligned} FV &= 40\,000\left(1 + \dfrac{0.012}{12}\right)^{120} \\ &= \$45\,097.17 \end{aligned}$$
criteria: Correct answer
Writes an expression for the future value with some correct element(s), or equivalent merit

solutions.latex:
For Option 2, quarterly deposits for 10 years give $N = 10 \times 4 = 40$.
$$r = \dfrac{2.4\%}{4} = \dfrac{0.024}{4} = 0.6\% = 0.006$$
The table factor for $N = 40$, $r = 0.6\%$ is $45.05630$.
$$\begin{aligned} FV &= 45.05630 \times 1000 \\ &= \$45\,056.30 \end{aligned}$$
Option 1 gives $\$45\,097.17$, so the difference is
$$\begin{aligned} 45\,097.17 - 45\,056.30 &= \$40.87 \end{aligned}$$
criteria: Correct answer
Calculates the future value using the interest factor table, or equivalent merit

options.label: B

parts.latex:
An annuity consists of ten payments, each equal to \$1000. Each payment is made on 30 June each year from 2021 through to 2030 inclusive.

The rate of compound interest is $5\%$ per annum.

The present value of the annuity is calculated at 30 June 2020.

The future value of the annuity is calculated at 30 June 2030.

Without performing any calculations, which of the following statements is true?

solutions.latex:
The payments total $10 \times \$1000 = \$10\,000$.

The present value is the value at 30 June 2020, before any payment is made. Each payment is discounted back, so each is worth less than \$1000 and the present value is less than \$10\,000.

The future value is the value at 30 June 2030. Every payment except the last has earned interest, so the future value is greater than \$10\,000.
$$\text{Present value} < \$10\,000 < \text{future value}$$
This is option A.
criteria: Correct answer

4512.stem:
Tina inherits \$60 000 and invests it in an account earning interest at a rate of $0.5\%$ per month. Each month, immediately after the interest has been paid, Tina withdraws \$800.

The amount in the account immediately after the $n$th withdrawal can be determined using the recurrence relation

$$A_n = A_{n-1}(1.005) - 800,$$

where $n = 1, 2, 3, \dots$ and $A_0 = 60\,000$.

parts.latex: Use the recurrence relation to find the amount of money in the account immediately after the third withdrawal.
Calculate the amount of interest earned in the first three months.

criteria: Correct answer
Finds the value of $A_1$, or equivalent merit

solutions.latex:
Total withdrawals after 3 months:
$$800\times 3 = \$2400$$
The balance has reduced by
$$60\,000-58\,492.49 = \$1507.51$$
Interest earned is the withdrawals minus the reduction:
$$\begin{aligned} I &= 2400-1507.51 \\ &= \$892.49 \end{aligned}$$
criteria: Correct answer
Finds by how much the balance is reduced, or equivalent merit

solutions.latex:
Present value of the \$1000 annuity for 20 years:
$$16.351\times 1000 = \$16\,351$$
The \$3000 payments are years 21 to 30, so take a 30-year annuity less a 20-year annuity:
$$\begin{aligned} \text{PV}_{30} &= 22.396\times 3000 = \$67\,188 \\ \text{PV}_{20} &= 16.351\times 3000 = \$49\,053 \end{aligned}$$
Total present value:
$$\begin{aligned} PV &= 16\,351+67\,188-49\,053 \\ &= \$34\,486 \end{aligned}$$
Alternate solution: the last 10 payments, discounted back 20 years, have present value
$$\dfrac{3000\times 8.983}{(1+0.02)^{20}}$$
$$\begin{aligned} \text{Total} &= 16.351\times 1000+\dfrac{3000\times 8.983}{(1+0.02)^{20}} \\ &= \$34\,486.90 \end{aligned}$$
criteria: Correct answer
Provides calculation for the value of the \$1000 annuity for 20 years, or equivalent merit
Identifies an appropriate annuity factor, or equivalent merit

parts.latex:
Julie invests $\$12\,500$ in a savings account. Interest is paid at a fixed monthly rate. At the end of each month, after the monthly interest is added, Julie makes a deposit of $\$500$.

Julie has created a spreadsheet to show the activity in her savings account. The details for the first 6 months are shown.

\extable{38_q21_t1}

By finding the monthly rate of interest, complete the final row above for the 7th month.

solutions.latex:
The month 1 interest is $\$18.75$ on a balance of $\$12\,500$, which gives the monthly rate.
$$\begin{aligned} \text{Monthly rate} &= \dfrac{18.75}{12\,500}\times 100\% \\ &= 0.15\% \end{aligned}$$
Interest for month 7 is on the opening balance.
$$\begin{aligned} \text{Interest} &= 15\,624.20\times 0.0015 \\ &\approx \$23.44 \end{aligned}$$
The final row is
$$\begin{array}{|c|c|c|c|c|} \hline 7 & 15\,624.20 & 23.44 & 500 & 16\,147.64 \\ \hline \end{array}$$
criteria: Correct answer
Calculates interest correctly, or equivalent merit
Calculates the monthly rate of interest, or equivalent merit

parts.latex:
Present value interest factors for an annuity of $\$1$ for various interest rates ($r$) and numbers of periods ($N$) are given in the table.

\extable{38_q31_t1}

A bank lends Martina $\$500\,000$ to purchase a home, with interest charged at 1.5% per annum compounding monthly. She agrees to repay the loan by making equal monthly repayments over a 30-year period.

How much should the monthly payment be in order to pay off the loan in 30 years? Give your answer correct to the nearest cent.

solutions.latex:
The monthly interest rate is
$$\begin{aligned} r &= \dfrac{0.015}{12} \\ &= 0.00125 = 0.125\% \end{aligned}$$
The number of periods is $N = 30\times 12 = 360$. The present value interest factor is read from the table for these values of $r$ and $N$.
$$\begin{aligned} \text{Monthly payment} &= \dfrac{500\,000}{289.75411} \\ &= \$1725.60 \text{ (nearest cent)} \end{aligned}$$
criteria: Correct answer
Identifies the correct present value interest factor, or divides $500\,000$ by any value

meta.format_note: Table value 289.75411 taken from source; table not visible to check.

parts.latex:
A table of future value interest factors for an annuity of $\$1$ is shown.

\extable{38_q40_t1}

Simone deposits $\$1000$ into a savings account at the end of each year for 8 years. The interest rate for these 8 years is 0.75% per annum, compounded annually.

After the 8th deposit, Simone stops making deposits but leaves the money in the savings account. The money in her savings account then earns interest at 1.25% per annum, compounded annually, for a further two years.

Find the amount of money in Simone’s savings account at the end of ten years.

solutions.latex:
The first 8 deposits form an annuity; the future value interest factor is read from the table.
$$\begin{aligned} \text{Amount after 8 years} &= 1000\times 8.2132 \\ &= \$8213.20 \end{aligned}$$
This then grows by compound interest at 1.25% for 2 years.
$$\begin{aligned} \text{Amount after 10 years} &= 8213.20(1.0125)^2 \\ &= \$8419.81 \end{aligned}$$
criteria: Correct answer
Finds the correct future value of the annuity and attempts to apply the compound interest formula, or equivalent merit
Identifies the correct interest factor from the table, or equivalent merit

4340.stem:
The table shows the future value for an annuity of \$1 for varying interest rates and time periods.

\extable{40_q20_t1}

parts.latex:
Ken invests \$200 at the start of each year for eight years, at an interest rate of $5\%$ per annum.

Calculate the future value of Ken's investment.

Shay is planning to take a holiday in three years. She needs \$4500 for this holiday and will make regular six-monthly payments into an account that earns interest at the rate of $4\%$ per annum, compounded 6 monthly.

What is the minimum amount Shay needs to pay into this account every 6 months? Give your answer to the nearest \$10. Support your answer with calculations.

solutions.latex:
Read the factor for $8$ periods at $5\%$ from the table.
$$\$200\times 10.0266=\$2005.32$$
criteria: Correct answer

solutions.latex:
The rate per six months is
$$r=\dfrac{4}{2}\%=2\%$$
The number of periods is
$$n=3\times 2=6$$
Using the table factor $6.4343$ for $2\%$ and $6$ periods:
$$\begin{aligned} \text{Investment per 6 months} &= \dfrac{4500}{6.4343} \\ &= 699.37\ldots \\ &\approx \$700 \text{ (to the nearest } \$10) \end{aligned}$$
criteria: Correct answer
Finds the correct rate, or equivalent merit

figures.cap: solution sketch: time line marking 0, 15 and 25 years

solutions.latex:
Monthly rate:

$$\begin{aligned} r &= \dfrac{2.4\%}{12} \\ &= 0.2\% \end{aligned}$$

\exfigure{40_q41_s1}

Treat the withdrawals as \$1200 per month for 25 years (300 months) plus an extra \$800 per month for the first 15 years (180 months).

$$\text{For 25 years: }1200\times 225.430=270\,516$$

$$\text{For 15 years, extra: }800\times 151.036=120\,828.80$$

$$\begin{aligned} \text{Total} &= 270\,516+120\,828.80 \\ &= \$391\,344.80 \end{aligned}$$
criteria: Correct answer
Makes substantial progress towards a solution, or equivalent merit
Demonstrates in calculations understanding of the importance of 15 years and 25 years, or equivalent merit
Identifies the required interest rate, or equivalent merit
